title: Azure NetApp Files - Simply Explained

entities.name: Azure NetApp Files
entities.quote: So why does Azure NetApp files even exist? That's the first question people ask when they hear about it.

entities.name: Azure Files
entities.quote: We'll cover what it actually is, the three main use cases where it shines and how it compares to Azure files.

entities.name: Microsoft Azure
entities.quote: Azure already gives you plenty of storage options, blob, files, disk.

entities.name: Azure Virtual Desktop
entities.quote: hosting Windows desktops in the cloud, think as you are virtual desktop or Citrix.

entities.name: Microsoft Entra ID
entities.quote: It uses EntraID for access control, snapshots handle backups, and replication covers disaster recovery.

quotes.text: The issue isn't that Azure files is bad. It's a great service for what it's designed to do. But it's optimized for cost. Not peak performance.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames the choice between the two services as cost versus peak performance rather than good versus bad.

quotes.text: Flexible service level changes that completely. It decouples capacity from throughput, two independent knobs instead of one. You decide how much storage you need and separately how much performance you need.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the key pricing change in a clear, intuitive way.

quotes.text: Azure NetApp files doesn't compete with Azure files. It fills a specific performance gap, a gap that matters for the right workloads.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Positions Azure NetApp Files precisely within the Azure storage portfolio.

quotes.text: One caution though, don't migrate everything to ANF just because it's fast. Use it where it matters most. For general file shares and everyday workloads, Azure files is still the right choice.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a practical recommendation against over-using premium storage.

chapters.title: Azure NetApp Files vs. Azure Files

takeaways: Azure NetApp Files is a first-party, fully managed Azure file service on NetApp technology that delivers sub-millisecond latency and very high throughput over SMB and NFS.
Its sweet spots are SAP HANA, high performance computing and VDI profile storage, while Azure Files remains the cost-effective choice for general file shares.
The flexible service level decouples capacity from throughput, so you no longer over-provision storage just to get the performance a workload needs.
hook: Some workloads simply cannot wait on storage: SAP HANA logs, large simulations and VDI logon storms. This episode explains for Azure architects and IT pros what Azure NetApp Files is, where it beats Azure Files, and how the flexible service level keeps high performance storage affordable.
